name: University of Copenhagen
about: The first thing to know about the University of Copenhagen, for anyone finishing an IB, is that you cannot study there at bachelor level without fluent academic Danish. UCPH says it plainly on its own bachelor page: "UCPH only offers bachelor's degree programmes taught in Danish." All 78 bachelor's degrees are in Danish; the English-taught offering begins at master's level. It was founded in 1479 and has about 36,800 students across six faculties and four campuses in and around central Copenhagen — and if you want it, you need to plan a Danish-language route into it years in advance, not in your final IB year.
ibNotes: UCPH accepts the IB Diploma with Diploma Programme (DP) Results as meeting the general admission requirement. An IB Certificate (DP Course Results) qualifies only with at least 18 points and grade 3 or above in all six courses, plus supplementary courses giving at least one A-level and one B-level subject.

There is a hard grade floor: "In addition to having accomplished an IB Diploma, you must present a grade point average equivalent to the Danish 6.0 – or more." Below a converted 6.0 you cannot be considered in quota 1.

IB holders can apply through both quota 1 and quota 2. UCPH states: "You are only eligible for admission through quota 1 if your upper secondary education is from within the EU or you have an International Baccalaureate (IB) or an European Baccalaureate (EB)."

Danish language is a requirement for every bachelor's degree. If your A HL/SL or B HL Language or Literature subject is not Danish, Norwegian or Swedish, you must pass Studieprøven i dansk som andetsprog or document equivalent academic Danish. Danish B at HL normally exempts you.

Studieprøven has four parts — oral, listening, reading and written — and "must be passed with at least grade 02 in each of all the 3 examination disciplines". Medicine, Dentistry and Dental Hygiene require grade 7 rather than 02 in each discipline. Alternatively you can pass a supplementary upper secondary course in Danish A.
Students from the Nordic countries with Danish, Norwegian or Swedish in their upper secondary education do not have to sit a Danish language test.

UCPH's IB results-service institution code is 002600. If you enrol straight after the IB, you must authorise online access to your results: "Please give your permission to your IB coordinator before 1 May."

Subject conversion follows the Danish Agency's handbook: IB Mathematics HL/SL counts as Matematik A/B, Physics HL/SL as Fysik A/B, English A1/A2 at SL or HL as Engelsk A, and Danish A1 HL as the Danish requirement.
quotaNotes: Quota 1 is a ranking on the converted grade point average from your first given exam certificate, and you need at least a converted 6.0 to be in it at all. Quota 2 at UCPH is not a paper exercise: applicants must sit and pass a quota 2 test and take part in an interview, and UCPH states that "Applicants who have not participated and passed the quota 2-test will not be considered for admission" in that quota. The interview is held in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish, which is a further reason the Danish requirement is not a formality. Quota 2 selection is an overall assessment of the test and the interview. The quota 2 application deadline is 15 March at 12:00; quota 1 applicants have until 5 July at 12:00. Offers are published on 28 July.

tuitionNonEu: Non-EU/EEA citizens pay tuition fees unless they hold a residence permit that exempts them. Rates are set per programme and were not published on the English bachelor pages checked. UCPH states: "The University of Copenhagen does not offer financial support or scholarships to foreign students."

notes: There are no fully English-taught bachelor's degrees at the University of Copenhagen. UCPH's own bachelor page reads: "Kickstart your career at UCPH and explore 78 bachelor's degree programmes - all are taught in Danish" and, separately, "UCPH only offers bachelor's degree programmes taught in Danish." The programmes list below is therefore empty, and that is the accurate answer rather than an omission.

This is a bachelor-level fact only. UCPH runs around 120 master's programmes, many of them in English, so Copenhagen is a realistic destination after a bachelor's degree elsewhere — including after an English-taught bachelor at CBS, DTU, AU, AAU, ITU or RUC.

If you genuinely want UCPH at bachelor level, the route is Danish. Either take Danish A as your IB Language A or B HL subject, or plan to pass Studieprøven i dansk som andetsprog. Studieprøven is normally reached after roughly two to three years of Danish courses, so this is a decision to take in the first year of the Diploma Programme at the latest.
The converted 6.0 GPA floor sits on top of the language requirement, not instead of it. Both have to be cleared.
Quota 2 at UCPH involves a test and an interview conducted in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish — a further reason why applying without the language is not viable.
A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. The 6.0 is a grade point average on the Danish 7-point scale.
Tuition fees for non-EU/EEA bachelor applicants are not confirmed here; ask UCPH.
